findings.text: Upheld (Q4, dead path). Checked: line 176 calls scopeOf(flags, ["workspace", "shared"]), and scopeOf (line 89) throws a UsageError for any value outside that list. So scope can never be "project" at line 177, and its throw never runs.

Upheld (Q4/Q9, dead path). Checked: createRepository is called only from openRepo (line 530), and only when create is given. With create, resolveRepo writes knowledge.json when it is missing or unreadable (resolve.ts:213-215, 232-237), or takes a folder only when its manifest parses as a project manifest (resolve.ts:155). So the !existsSync(MANIFEST_FILE) branch cannot be reached.

Upheld (Q2, duplicated logic). Checked: lines 661-665 compare git versions by major and minor by hand. The same rule already exists as older() with GIT_MIN_VERSION in repo.ts:293/320, which compares all three parts. The two give the same answer today only because GIT_MIN_VERSION is [2, 32, 0].

Upheld (Q9/Q6, a fallback that hides a cause). Checked: the bare catch replaces any scanRepos failure with the unmapped listing. A SQL or read error is then swallowed, and the line can still report ok. The surrounding knowledge() wrapper (line 823) would otherwise have reported it as a warning.
Kept as advisory (Q10/Q6): runChecks's doc comment now sits above the Knowledge section and describes the wrong unit.
Kept as advisory (Q9): the bare catch around the over_cap query; the reviewer graded it advisory.
Kept as advisory (Q2): isDirectory is written a third time. This is boilerplate, not logic.
Kept as advisory (Q2): projectFolders and foldersByHand copy the module's folder listing.
Kept as advisory (Q2): adopt repeats underLeases's lease nesting.
Kept as advisory (Q6): requireGit branches on the message text (TIMED_OUT) instead of an error code.
Kept as advisory (Q9): a decided proposal with no decision key is read as rejected without a problem. The data gate notes the same at the same line.
Kept as advisory (Q4/Q5): folderName and GitOptions.timeoutMs are knobs that only tests use.
Kept as advisory (Q8): moduleVersion and readEntry are exports nothing outside tests imports; the rubric grades this advisory.
Kept as advisory (Q9): the ?? "" fallback is for a key the map always holds.
Kept as advisory (Q11), at the reviewer's grade: the ADR says move, restore and compact 'wait for a write', but the code refuses them, as AC-19 says. Correct the ADR's sentence.
Lowered to advisory, debt: the line is outside the change.

Upheld (Q1, AC-18 'a caller cannot set an entry's id'). Checked: no knowledge test passes an id in a change to writeEntry. The test at line 831 covers only the other half of AC-18 (an entry id that belongs to another slug). Today only the EntryChange type keeps a caller's id out. A runtime change that let a caller's id through would pass every test.

Upheld (Q1, AC-15 'title, context, subject and body are passed through redact'). Checked: the test puts a secret only in body and context. Removing the clean() call on title (store.ts:461) or on subject (store.ts:465) leaves every test passing. The redacted title also feeds the slug (store.ts:468).
Kept as advisory: at this level only the version probe times out. The runner-level test still covers the timeout in runGit.
Kept as advisory: AC-8's 'killed' is asserted only through the 'timed out' message.
Kept as advisory (Q5): the parent-repository check is weak. The ceiling-directory guard is held by the environment test at line 395.
Kept as advisory: no test reads a log line to check that stderr is clipped there.
Kept as advisory: the test of 'gains a remote' is resolved through the row, not the manifest. The lost-rows test at line 99 covers the manifest path.
Kept as advisory (Q8), at the reviewer's grade: fixtures use personal names, including the owner's real name. A neutral name would do.

Upheld (Q1, boundary). checkRepoConfig reads only .git/config as text. Git also reads the repository configuration through a .git/commondir file, and reads .git/config.worktree when extensions.worktreeConfig is set; the extensions section is not refused. Neither path is checked, and configArgs (line 225) does not override filter.*. A [filter] clean= program with a matching .gitattributes line therefore runs on the engine's git add and on doctor's git status. That breaks the refusal AC-15 and AC-19 promise for a repository configuration that could run a program. This is the stated guarantee, not hardening beyond it.

Upheld (Q1, boundary). Checked: when .git is a gitfile, headOf returns null because isDirectory uses lstat (line 550). openRepo then skips checkRepoConfig (line 529), and createRepository runs git init (line 472), which reinitialises the repository the gitfile points to. The later --git-dir add and commit land in that outside repository under its unchecked configuration. At line 532, checkRepoConfig fails to read .git/config with ENOTDIR and returns silently (line 371). This breaks AC-2 and AC-15, and it repeats on every write.
Kept as advisory (A-1, hardening): the temp file write follows a symlink already at the .tmp name.
Kept as advisory (A-2, hardening): checkTarget checks only the last path component; a symlinked parent folder is followed.
Kept as advisory (A-3, hardening): restoreKept writes through a symlink.
Kept as advisory (A-4, hardening): paths read back from git are passed as pathspecs, which glob. GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 would pin them.
Kept as advisory (A-5, hardening): doctor reads knowledge.json with readFileSync, not readRegularFile.

Advisory (personal-data, filed by the reviewer under Not answerable): the reviewer could not settle the erasure question for the author name in commits. The data gate upholds it as a defect at 0006_knowledge_store.sql:45.
Lowered to advisory, debt: backup code the diff did not touch. It now carries knowledge rows to the configured backup target.

Upheld (Q3 irreversible overwrite, Q1 seen only in a log). Checked: revertInterrupted calls restoreToHead on the intent's paths without comparing their current content. That runs git restore --worktree from HEAD and rmSync on created paths (line 642). An edit the person made after the interruption and before the next openRepo, which any knowledge command triggers, adopt included, is destroyed for good. Line 811 only writes a log line. This contradicts spec.md:314, which says the person's hand edits are never touched by the revert and that the revert is reported.

Upheld (Q3/Q1). Checked: for an interrupted adopt, a changed status triggers restoreKept (line 803, write at 774), which writes the bytes kept at adopt time over the files. A later hand edit is silently replaced, and only the log line at 811 records it. This contradicts spec.md:314.
Kept as advisory: the module migration pass is not contained, and doctor does not warn when the module schema is 'behind'.
Kept as advisory: the rollback is stated with its reason but is manual. The only backup before the drop shares BACKUPS_KEPT = 2 with core backups. The rubric grades a manual rollback advisory.
Lowered to advisory, debt: the upgrade runner's 10 s wait already existed before this item.

Upheld (Q5/Q2: the Design is built only in part). spec.md:240 says 'the knowledge store refuses to read or write with ModuleSchemaTooNewError', and spec.md:147 lists the refusal as step 1. Checked: requireSchema is called only by the write functions in store.ts and taxonomy.ts. rebuildAll (514), ensureFresh (553) and listRepos/saveRow never call it, and the CLI (knowledge.ts:297) never checks it. So knowledge rebuild and knowledge list delete and rewrite rows in tables a newer binary owns.
Kept as advisory: the manifest's aliases are extended outside a commit. The ADR names this as a known limit.
Kept as advisory: two function-level import cycles (repo↔resolve, repo↔author).
Kept as advisory: doctor builds a store by hand with db as Db and re-implements the module's layout and version rule. The code-quality gate upholds the version-rule copy separately.
Kept as advisory: the readFileSync there follows a symlink, against the Design's lstat/O_NOFOLLOW rule.
Kept as advisory: runChecks's doc comment was moved.
Kept as advisory: WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_AUTHOR is missing from the viewer's SettingKey type. This follows the precedent of WIZARDINGCODE_MODULES.
Lowered to advisory, debt: ADR 0019 is outside the change and has no forward reference to ADR 0024.

Upheld (Q3: the order of steps around the transaction, a row loss a reader can name). Checked: rebuildRepo reads the files at line 457, but takes headOf and fingerprintOf only inside the transaction (lines 491-492). A file added or renamed in that gap is counted in the recorded fingerprint and missing from the rows. ensureFresh (line 559) then sees a match and never rebuilds, so the entry stays absent from the index until the folder changes again. Taking the head and fingerprint before readRepoFiles fixes it. settle/recordRepoNow (lines 158-159) has the same order.

Upheld (Q5: personal data in a column with no stated retention). knowledge_entries.author and knowledge_proposals.proposed_by/decided_by (lines 67-69) hold a person's name, and the same name goes into commits that are never rewritten. Checked: ADR 0024 has no retention or erasure text. spec.md:322 says only where the data lives. The project states retention elsewhere (compact, history forget).

Kept as advisory: the destructive drop has a stated reason (line 5, ADR 0024:119, O-1), and a VACUUM INTO backup runs first. That backup is pruned by BACKUPS_KEPT = 2. The probe (probes/withdrawn-module-objects.md) settles the open question: the withdrawn module made no views, and its three triggers are on knowledge_entries only, so the drop removes them with the table. The test does not create the triggers, so that part rests on SQLite's rule, not on a run.
Kept as advisory: the two indexes dropped from the core table injections belonged to the withdrawn module, and no core query uses them. The SQL comment does not say so.
Kept as advisory: on stores that ran the withdrawn module, the first open takes a one-time VACUUM INTO under the write lock. The spec and the ADR state this.
Kept as advisory, at the reviewer's grade: the file: and dup: ids leave out the folder, so the same name in open/ and decided/ collides under INSERT OR REPLACE.
Kept as advisory (Q4): a missing decision key is indexed as rejected, with no problem shown.
Kept as advisory (Q2): a LIKE prefix scan on a small table.
Kept as advisory (Q2): project_aliases is read by project_id with no index; the table is small and the read is off the hook path.
Lowered to advisory, debt: the missing project_id index on project_aliases predates the change.
